title: CLO 2026.0 - Mode & Editor
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! CLO technical experts provide a detailed explanation of the pattern & editor related feature updates: calculating and displaying the average consumption and weight per garment, supporting same-piece same-direction in two-way or four-way nesting, adding an outer line option for nesting calculation, supporting point-to-point distance measurement, and shortcut keys for rotating pattern pieces.
transcript:
This video will introduce the functions related to the mode and editor to help you improve.

First of all, there are improvements in printing and distribution. We have significantly improved the cost and calculation process.

In this update, you can now automatically calculate the average production of each piece of clothing based on the material data and monitor the cost of each piece.

This update makes it easier for you to calculate and manage production costs directly within the software.

If you want to check the cost information, please click on the material list under the top main menu.

You will see that the central fabric project list screen has been newly added to the single-click cost list on the right.

Below the number, there is also a gray number showing the quantity of each piece.

Open printing and distribution, then click on the material setting icon in the toolbar.

You will then see the information menu.

Under the information menu, the average length of each piece of clothing has been newly added.

Set the print number to 5 and the width to 1200 mm.

Click on the print all fabric icon to print.

Check the value again; you will see that it has been updated according to the print result.

To match the final cost, open the material list editor again.

You will see the cost of each piece of fabric, which has been calculated based on the material data just processed in the print distribution.

At this point, I want to modify the fabric price and unit.

You can find the small ruler icon at the top.

Enter the user-defined settings and choose to modify it to RMB.

Change the volume unit to meters.

Adjust the price per meter.

At this time, the total cost has been updated.

For the unit cost, you need to click on the update button in the upper left corner to apply the update.

Adjust the price of another piece of fabric and update.

From this version, when you print, the line direction can be set to two or four directions.

You can set the same-piece clothing to have the same direction.

This function ensures that all pieces of the same clothing maintain the same line direction.

First, open the print settings.

Let's change the line direction in the attribute editor to either two or four directions.

The same-piece and same-piece options that were previously in use can now be used.

Click to open this option.

Then set the number of clothing items as the number of units.

Select the number of units to be divided.

Set the number of number keys that need to be entered.

Here I will enter two keys, XSM and XL.

Click on the print icon to start printing.

After printing is finished,

Open the display number random color in the vertical menu bar.

And display the size of the numbers.

This is convenient for checking the direction of the clothing.

Although the overall print aligns with the set line direction,

You can see that all pieces of the same clothing also maintain the same direction.

Now you can choose from the attribute editor in the print settings.

Click on the print icon.

Now you can choose from the attribute editor in the print settings.

In the editor,

Choose to set the print line,

Print line or base line as reference lines for efficient print execution.

Click on the print setting.

You can find it in the attribute editor.

The new print calculation menu is in the print settings.

You can use the download menu to select the reference line you need.

At this time, print is selected.

You can see that the print result is calculated according to the selected print line.

When the print has a print line,

It will also default to the print line.

Now set the option to print line.

Execute the print again.

You will see that the print is calculated according to the print line.

The last option is the base line.

Since the external CAD print is imported as DXF format,

The print is displayed in the form of a base line.

Select this option and run the print.

The print will run according to the base line set in the print.

So in this case,

Use the base line option to make an exact print.

Switch back to the print option and print again.

Select the print line,

Then the different print options underneath.

Press the breath while holding down the Eden onboarding.

Now select includes,

From the command bar,

To send a print pattern to the print set.

Once the exact measurement distance is displayed, only one measurement value is shown at a time.

When you click on another point, the previous measurement value will be automatically deleted, and a new measurement will start.

Once again, click on the roll icon to exit this function.

Finally, I will introduce the shortcut key to add a rotating board.

After clicking on the board, the mouse will stop on the rotation option in the menu.

You can see that each rotation direction and angle corresponds to a shortcut key.

Please select a board that needs to be rotated one or more times.

Press the Ctrl key and press the right arrow key to rotate the board clockwise 45 degrees.

Press the left arrow key to rotate the board counterclockwise 45 degrees.

When you want to rotate at a larger angle, you can press the right arrow key to rotate counterclockwise 90 degrees,

or press the left arrow key to rotate counterclockwise 90 degrees.

When you want to rotate at a larger angle, you can press the right arrow key to rotate counterclockwise 90 degrees.

When you want to rotate at a larger angle, you can press the right arrow key to rotate counterclockwise 90 degrees.

This is a guide to help you work in the animation environment and improve accuracy.

Animation Time Rectangle Marker

In animation projects, time control is important.

These markers are like numbers on the time axis.

Let's learn how to use these markers to simplify your production process.

First, we need to go to the bottom of the screen.

We need to enter the animation editor at the bottom of the screen.

Check the time axis and the area that shows your real number.

If you want to add a precise moment to view and mark the animation,

All you need to do is right-click on the time axis and click on the animation mark group in the right-click menu.

At this time, an animation mark dialog box will pop up.

You can specify a specific name for the mark here.

For example, from here, and you can set a precise real number.

After pressing OK, hover the mouse over the mark indicator.

You will see a pop-up window.

It contains a specific name and position for quick reference.

If you want to edit the animation mark,

You can right-click it and select Edit or double-click.

By dragging the mark, you can adjust its position.

To copy, paste and delete the animation mark,

You can right-click the animation mark again and select the desired operation.

Or use the shortcuts Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V, and Delete to speed up the process.

This is how to use the new animation mark to organize your animation

and better communicate with your team.

You can ensure that every frame in the animation is in its proper position.

I hope this video helps you.

Thank you for watching.

See you next time.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Mode & Editor
chunks.content: ## CLO 2026.0 Mode & Editor Overview This document covers the new features and improvements in CLO 2026.0 related to mode settings, editor enhancements, printing, cost calculation, fabric management, print line direction, rotation shortcuts, and animation time markers. It explains technical procedures, user interface updates, and workflow optimizations designed to improve accuracy and efficiency in garment production and animation projects. --- ## Printing and Cost Calculation Improvements This section explains enhancements to printing and distribution functions, including automatic average production calculations and cost monitoring per garment piece, optimized for production cost management within CLO software. - **Automatic Cost Calculation:** The update enables automatic calculation of the average production cost per clothing piece based on material data. - **Accessing Cost Information:** Users can click on the material list under the main top menu to view the central fabric project list and a newly added single-click cost list on the right. - **Quantity Display:** Below each item number, a gray number shows the quantity of each piece. - **Material Settings:** Clicking the material setting icon in the toolbar opens the information menu, where the average length per clothing piece is now displayed. - **Print Setup Example:** Set print number to 5 and width to 1200 mm, then use the "print all fabric" icon to execute printing. - **Cost Updates:** After printing, cost values update automatically based on the print results. - **Material List Editor:** Reopening the material list editor shows the updated cost of each fabric piece calculated from the print distribution data. --- ## Fabric Price and Unit Modification This section details how to customize fabric price units and update costs dynamically within the software. - **Accessing Unit Settings:** A small ruler icon at the top opens user-defined settings. - **Currency and Units:** Users can change currency (e.g., to RMB) and volume units (e.g., meters). - **Price Adjustment:** Input a new price per meter, which triggers an automatic update to the total cost. - **Applying Changes:** Click the update button in the upper left corner to apply unit cost changes. - **Multiple Fabric Updates:** Adjust prices for different fabrics individually and update accordingly. --- ## Print Line Direction Settings This section describes the new ability to set line direction in printing, ensuring consistent orientation for all pieces of the same garment. - **Line Directions:** Users can choose two or four directions for line orientation during printing. - **Same-Piece Direction:** Option to maintain the same line direction across all pieces of the same clothing. - **Setup Procedure:** - Open print settings and access the attribute editor. - Change line direction to two or four directions. - Enable "same-piece" options. - Enter the number of clothing units and specify keys (e.g., XSM, XL) for size division. - **Verification:** After printing, use "display number random color" from the vertical menu bar to visualize size and direction alignment.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Mode & Editor
chunks.content: - **Same-Piece Direction:** Option to maintain the same line direction across all pieces of the same clothing. - **Setup Procedure:** - Open print settings and access the attribute editor. - Change line direction to two or four directions. - Enable "same-piece" options. - Enter the number of clothing units and specify keys (e.g., XSM, XL) for size division. - **Verification:** After printing, use "display number random color" from the vertical menu bar to visualize size and direction alignment. --- ## Reference Lines for Printing This section explains how to use print line and base line references for precise print execution, especially useful when importing external CAD prints. - **Print Line Options:** Users can select either "print line" or "base line" as reference lines in the attribute editor under print settings. - **Print Calculation Menu:** Available in print settings allows selection of the reference line type. - **Print Line Reference:** When selected, printing aligns according to the print line. - **Base Line Reference:** Used primarily for prints imported in DXF format, enabling exact printing based on the baseline. - **Switching Between Options:** Users can toggle between print line and base line options to fit different print requirements. --- ## Measurement and Pattern Printing Commands This section covers commands related to precise measurement display and print pattern management. - **Measurement Display:** When measuring distances on prints, only one measurement value shows at a time; selecting a new point deletes the previous measurement. - **Exiting Measurement Mode:** Click the roll icon to exit measurement functions. - **Print Pattern Command:** From the command bar, use the "includes" command to send a print pattern to the print set for execution. --- ## Rotation Shortcuts for Boards This section outlines shortcut keys to efficiently rotate boards within the editor, supporting quick orientation adjustments. - **Rotation Menu:** After selecting a board, hovering over the rotation option displays corresponding shortcut keys. - **Shortcut Keys:** - **Ctrl + Right Arrow:** Rotate board clockwise by 45 degrees. - **Ctrl + Left Arrow:** Rotate board counterclockwise by 45 degrees. - **Right Arrow (without Ctrl):** Rotate board clockwise by 90 degrees. - **Left Arrow (without Ctrl):** Rotate board counterclockwise by 90 degrees. - **Use Case:** Enables fast rotation for multiple boards to improve layout accuracy. --- ## Animation Time Rectangle Marker This section introduces animation time markers, tools for precise time control and organization within animation projects. - **Accessing Animation Editor:** Located at the bottom of the screen, showing the time axis and real number area. - **Adding Animation Marks:** - Right-click the time axis. - Select "animation mark group" from the context menu. - In the dialog box, assign a specific name (e.g., "from here") and a precise real number timestamp. - **Using Animation Marks:** - Hovering over a mark shows its name and position. - Marks can be edited by right-clicking or double-clicking. - Dragging adjusts mark position. - **Managing Marks:** Copy, paste, and delete operations available via right-click menu or shortcuts: Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V, and Delete.

These features provide users with refined control over material management, print accuracy, and animation timeline organization.
